doc.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe Interview, 1961-11-25
doc.interviewee: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe

title: Jazz as American, with the best bands from New Orleans
summary: Russell argues that jazz developed in America and that most of the better bands originated in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Oh yes, it seemed to be something definitely developed in America, and I'm ready to believe from what I've seen and heard, that most of the better bands did originate here. Right in New Orleans. Right in New Orleans. There's been just entirely too many musicians here to say that, well, it's probably just the ones you heard of here. The ones that became famous happened to be born here, but there were so many here compared to other cities. There was nothing to compare with them in the north where I was raised, in other towns. I didn't have the experience of being all over the country, and maybe even early enough to hear the bands, what was happening in New York. But judging from the phonograph records and other things that we'd been able to pin down, there was nothing up there that had the real jazz element in it in the beginning. Thank you.
